text.title: Ramp Task Difficulty Ladder Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules every ramp task difficulty ladder application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: Each rung MUST be defined by an observable scope of change (files touched, modules crossed, whether the change ships behind a feature flag, whether a design review is required), never by story points, T-shirt size, "easy / medium / hard" or the assigning engineer's opinion. A ticket is placed on a rung by matching its scope to the rung's `Ticket pattern` column; if two rungs match, the higher one applies.

rationale.source: Widely established practice in engineering onboarding; GitHub `good first issue` label guidance

rule.rationale: Story points encode how familiar the estimator is with the code, not how hard the task is for someone who has never seen it. A "2-point" ticket that touches the billing module and the deploy pipeline is a rung-4 task for a newcomer. Scope-based patterns let a buddy classify a ticket in under a minute and let two buddies reach the same rung.

rule.statement: The ladder MUST have at least 4 ordered rungs. Every rung MUST carry an `Expected duration` band, and the bands MUST be non-decreasing up the ladder: the upper bound of rung N is never greater than the upper bound of rung N+1. Rung 1 MUST have an upper bound of one working day or less; the top rung MUST fit inside the team's ramp window (10 working days for a 2-week ramp).

rationale.source: Vygotsky, zone of proximal development; Ericsson et al., deliberate practice (Psychological Review, 1993)

rule.rationale: A ladder whose rungs are not ordered by effort is a list, and a newcomer handed a task with no duration expectation has no way to know whether they are stuck or on pace. Rung 1 under a day is what makes the first day end with something merged, which is the single strongest predictor teams report for a newcomer's confidence in week one.

rule.statement: Rung 1 tickets MUST be real changes that merge to the main branch and ship through the normal pipeline (a docs fix, a dependency bump, a log line): not a sandbox exercise, a throwaway kata, or a change on a branch nobody merges. The outcome review records the newcomer's first merged PR date as `time_to_first_pr`; the ladder is out of tolerance when the median exceeds 3 working days.

rationale.source: Widely established practice in engineering onboarding (time-to-first-commit metric)

rule.rationale: A "training repo" teaches the newcomer the training repo. The value of rung 1 is that it exercises the actual clone, build, test, review and deploy path on day one, so the first thing that breaks is the onboarding doc, not the newcomer's first feature in week three.

rule.statement: Every rung MUST name its `Buddy support` level, and the level MUST decrease monotonically up the ladder: rung 1 is full pairing, the top rung is scheduled check-ins only. A rung MUST NOT specify less support than the rung below it, and no rung may specify "none" while the newcomer is inside the ramp window.

rationale.source: Collins, Brown and Newman, Cognitive Apprenticeship (1989), the fading principle

rule.rationale: Support that does not fade produces a newcomer who can only work while paired; support that drops to zero at rung 2 produces a newcomer who stalls silently for three days rather than admit it. The ladder is the contract that makes the fading explicit, so the buddy and the newcomer both know what "on my own" means at each rung.

rule.statement: Each rung's `Evidence link` MUST point at a merged PR or closed ticket that a previous newcomer completed on that rung, with the actual duration recorded next to it. A backlog item nobody has done, a senior engineer's PR, or "TBD" is not evidence. A rung with no prior completion MUST be marked `not_applicable: unvalidated` and its duration band treated as a guess until the next ramp fills it.

rationale.source: Widely established practice in evidence-based process improvement

rule.rationale: Duration bands invented at a whiteboard are wrong in the same direction every time: the people who wrote them already know the codebase. The only calibration that counts is a real newcomer's actual duration on a real ticket, which is why the ladder stays a hypothesis until one ramp has run through it.

rule.statement: Before the newcomer's start date the buddy MUST tag at least 2 candidate tickets per rung in the team's tracker with a rung label (for example `ramp/rung-1`), reserved from the sprint's committed scope. Rung 1 and rung 2 tickets MUST NOT sit on the sprint's critical path or carry a delivery deadline inside the ramp window.

rationale.source: GitHub `good first issue` label guidance; widely established practice in sprint planning

rule.rationale: The failure is always the same: the start date arrives, the buddy searches the backlog live, and the newcomer's day one is spent watching someone scroll Jira. Ramp tickets that carry a deadline get pulled by a senior engineer the moment the sprint slips, which strips the ladder from the bottom exactly when it is needed.

rule.statement: A newcomer moves to rung N+1 only after merging at least one ticket on rung N. Rungs MUST NOT be skipped, regardless of seniority or team pressure. If a ticket runs past twice its rung's expected upper bound, the buddy MUST review the ticket's classification (it is usually mis-rung) and re-label it, rather than record the overrun as a judgement of the newcomer.

rationale.source: Vygotsky, zone of proximal development; widely established practice in engineering onboarding

rule.rationale: "They are senior, give them the migration" is how an experienced hire spends their first week reverse-engineering a deploy pipeline nobody documented. The ladder's value is the ordered exposure to the team's specific systems; seniority shortens each rung, it does not remove them. Treating overruns as classification bugs keeps the ladder honest and keeps the newcomer from being graded by a guess.

rule.statement: The outcome review (at the published cadence, quarterly at most) MUST record per newcomer: `time_to_first_pr`, the rung reached on the last day of the ramp window, and actual versus expected duration per rung. Any rung whose median actual duration falls outside its expected band across the reviewed ramps MUST be re-banded or have its ticket pattern rewritten, and the ladder version bumped. A review that changes nothing after two consecutive cycles of out-of-band durations is invalid.

rationale.source: Deming PDCA cycle; widely established engineering-onboarding metrics (time to first PR, ramp completion)

rule.rationale: Without the regrade the ladder drifts away from the codebase it describes: the "single-file rename" rung becomes a two-day task once the monorepo grows, and every newcomer looks slow against a band set two years ago. The review is where the ladder learns from the ramps it produced.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit an artefact passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions hold.

rule.statement: Skip; surface the missing precondition; do not synthesize.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.
